extracted.intended_audience: journalism researchers, media scholars, and public relations/press officers interested in press-release pickup
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and empirical metrics for assessing how likely an organizational press release is to initiate news coverage and have its content reproduced across different types of news outlets. Based on large-scale automated content analysis of Dutch press releases and news output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article initiation (was the news article initiated by the release?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary/boolean pickup metric: whether a newspaper article in the sample was initiated by an organizational press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary pickup measure in the study; headline finding: approximately 10% of newspaper articles were initiated by releases (higher rates for the national news agency). This metric distinguishes agenda-initiation from mere reuse of wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literal reproduction fraction (what fraction of the release's literal content was reproduced?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative metric: the fraction of a press release's literal text that is reproduced verbatim in a news item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure direct textual uptake. Findings show higher reproduction at news agencies, tabloids, and free papers; quality papers reproduce less verbatim though they may still take agenda cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire-first targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reaching the national news agency (e.g., ANP, AP, Reuters, PA) is more pickup-effective than sending releases directly to individual papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical evidence shows agency routing increases both initiation and reproduction. Recommendation: prioritize distribution to news agencies when seeking broad pickup and verbatim reproduction at downstream outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabloid-and-free-paper targeting for high reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the goal is high literal reproduction of release content, target tabloids and free-distribution outlets, which reproduce NGO content more readily than quality papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NGO releases had higher reproduction rates at agencies, tabloids, and free papers. For high verbatim uptake, craft shorter, vivid releases suited to tabloid/free formats and consider NGO-specific messaging where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality-paper agenda hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality newspapers rarely reproduce verbatim but will take agenda cues from releases; to gain pickup at quality papers, the release must present a substantive story (detail, data, named expert) that enables independent reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality papers screen releases and prefer exclusives, unique data, or access to named experts. Releases aimed at quality outlets should emphasize original reporting opportunities, methodological detail, and spokesperson availability rather than copy-ready text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-type signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: The institutional source type (e.g., NGO vs. corporation) matters; releases should clearly signal sponsorship and methodology because quality-paper editors apply heavier scrutiny to NGO claims and downgrade releases that obscure these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sponsorship, funding, and methodological details explicit to avoid editorial downgrading; tailor transparency to match the receiving outlet's standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat-release / news-wave timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup is highest when a release is part of an ongoing news wave (i.e., repeated or temporally clustered releases) rather than an isolated one-off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal analysis shows follow-up and sustained messaging increase chance of initiation and reproduction. Plan releases as part of a sequence/wave rather than a single isolated outreach when seeking substantive pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-outlet differential framing (re-versioning)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single release can be re-versioned for different outlet tiers: tabloid version (short, vivid), agency version (factual, embeddable), and quality-paper version (data-rich, with named experts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce tailored versions for each target tier rather than one generic release; adjusting tone, length, and included materials improves pickup and appropriate reuse across outlet types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embeddability (supply auto-embeddable content blocks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases that provide embeddable content blocks (statistics tables, image carousels, pull quotes) increase reproduction at agencies and tabloid targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ready-to-use assets and modular content to facilitate verbatim reproduction and quick publishing by agencies and outlets with limited resources or tight deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality/exclusivity signals for quality papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality papers are more likely to 'pick up' a release if it offers exclusivity: an exclusive interview, first-look at an embargoed report, or access to a unique data set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To attract quality outlets, offer unique access or exclusives rather than copy-ready text; emphasize novelty and provide the evidence or access that enables independent reporting.
